guitar_overdrive|81 Creations Drive: Model of the 1981 Inventions DRV, a modern boutique drive with a punchy, amp-like mid push and wide gain range. Great for tightening high-gain amps or as a gritty, articulate crunch into a clean amp.
guitar_overdrive|Brit Blues: Model of the Marshall Bluesbreaker pedal: low-to-medium gain, transparent, slightly scooped 'amp-in-a-box' breakup. Ideal for bluesy edge-of-breakup tones or a gentle push into an already driven amp.
guitar_overdrive|Brit Governor: Model of the Marshall Guv'nor, a 'Marshall stack in a box' distortion with an active EQ. Use it to turn a clean amp into classic British crunch and rock rhythm.
guitar_overdrive|Chief BD2: Model of the BOSS BD-2 Blues Driver: dynamic, touch-sensitive overdrive that cleans up with picking and volume. A go-to for edge-of-breakup blues and roots tones.
guitar_overdrive|Chief DS1: Model of the BOSS DS-1, the classic orange distortion with a bright, raspy, scooped voice. Good for punk, grunge and '80s rock rhythm, or as a cutting lead boost.
guitar_overdrive|Chief MT: Model of the BOSS MT-2 Metal Zone: high-gain distortion with a powerful semi-parametric mid EQ. Use for saturated metal tones straight into a clean amp, or dial the mids for surgical voicing.
guitar_overdrive|Chief OD1: Model of the BOSS OD-1, the first compact overdrive pedal: smooth, asymmetric, mid-forward clipping. Great as a vintage-flavoured boost into a crunchy amp.
guitar_overdrive|Chief SD1: Model of the BOSS SD-1 Super OverDrive, a Tube Screamer cousin with asymmetric clipping. Classic choice to tighten and push a high-gain amp for metal rhythm.
guitar_overdrive|Exotic: Model of the Xotic BB Preamp: a smooth, open overdrive with lots of headroom and a two-band active EQ. Useful as an always-on 'amp-like' drive or a clean-ish solo boost.
guitar_overdrive|Exotic Z Boost: Model of the Xotic RC Booster: a clean, transparent boost with active bass/treble EQ. Adds volume and a little extra gain for solos without changing your core tone much.
guitar_overdrive|Facial Fuzz: Model of the Dunlop Fuzz Face: a fat, round, vintage two-transistor fuzz that cleans up with your guitar's volume knob. Perfect for Hendrix-style leads and '60s rock tones.
guitar_overdrive|Freeman BOD: Model of the Friedman BE-OD, which packs the Friedman BE-100 high-gain voice into a pedal. Use it for aggressive modern rock crunch into a clean or lightly driven amp.
guitar_overdrive|Fuzz Pi: Model of the Electro-Harmonix Big Muff Pi: thick, sustaining, scooped fuzz with a violin-like decay. Built for wall-of-sound rhythm, stoner rock and singing leads.
guitar_overdrive|Green 808: Model of the Ibanez TS808 Tube Screamer: mid-humped, soft-clipping overdrive. The classic tool to tighten the low end and push a high-gain amp, or for warm blues lead.
guitar_overdrive|MK3 Silicon Fuzz: Model of the JHS Bender 1973 London, a silicon Tone Bender MkIII-style fuzz. Gives a raspy, aggressive '70s British fuzz with more bite than germanium designs.
guitar_overdrive|Myth Drive: Model of the Klon Centaur: a mild, transparent overdrive that blends clean signal with clipped signal. Beloved as a clean boost/light drive that adds mids and sparkle without masking the amp.
guitar_overdrive|No-Bell OD1: Model of the Nobels ODR-1: a warm, natural overdrive with a distinctive mid voicing and 'Spectrum' tone control. A Nashville session favourite for smooth, full-bodied drive.
guitar_overdrive|Obsessive Drive: Model of the Fulltone OCD: a versatile overdrive/distortion that ranges from light crunch to amp-like rock saturation. Great for turning a clean amp into a British-flavoured rock rig.
guitar_overdrive|OD250: Model of the DOD Overdrive Preamp 250: a simple, gritty op-amp drive with a slightly raw, edgy character. Good for vintage crunch and as a boost with some grit.
guitar_overdrive|Rage Booster: Model of the Dallas Rangemaster treble booster. Pushes upper mids and treble into a driven amp for classic '60s/'70s British lead tones (Clapton, May, Iommi).
guitar_overdrive|Red Drive: Model of the Keeley Red Dirt, a modded Tube Screamer-style drive with more gain and a fuller low end. Use as an always-on crunch or a tightening boost for rock.
guitar_overdrive|Rodent Drive: Model of the ProCo RAT: gritty hard-clipping distortion with a unique Filter control. Covers everything from bluesy crunch to buzzy fuzz-like grind; loved in grunge and alt-rock.
guitar_overdrive|Thunderpaw: Model of the Mr Black Thunderclaw, a vintage Tone Bender MkI-style fuzz with a raw, splatty, ripping character. For garage rock and '60s psych fuzz tones.
guitar_overdrive|Vemural Ray: Model of the Vemuram Jan Ray: a transparent, dynamic 'Blackface Fender in a box' overdrive. Ideal for sparkly edge-of-breakup and a touch-sensitive always-on drive.
bass_overdrive|BDDI: Model of the Tech 21 SansAmp Bass Driver DI: amp-style preamp, drive and DI in one. The studio/live staple for gritty, punchy bass straight to the desk.
bass_overdrive|Exotic Bass Z Boost: Model of the Xotic RC Bass Booster: a clean boost with active EQ tailored to bass. Adds level and shape for fills or a fuller bass presence.
bass_overdrive|Douglas MT 3K: Model of the Darkglass Microtubes B3K: aggressive, modern bass distortion that blends drive with the clean low end. The go-to for metal and punchy grind bass.
bass_overdrive|Douglas Vintage MT: Model of the Darkglass Vintage Microtubes: a warmer, more vintage-flavoured bass overdrive with blend. Good for classic rock grit that keeps the bass fundamental intact.
bass_overdrive|Soviet Fuzz: Model of the Electro-Harmonix 'Russian' Big Muff: darker, bassier, smoother fuzz than the US version. A favourite for fuzz bass and fat stoner/doom guitar.
delay|Analog Delay: Neural DSP emulation of a bucket-brigade analog delay: warm, darkened repeats that degrade as they decay. Great for sitting behind leads without cluttering the mix.
delay|Slapback Delay: Short single-repeat delay voiced for classic rockabilly and country slapback. Adds depth and thickness to rhythm and chicken-picking parts.
delay|Digital Delay: Clean, pristine digital delay with accurate repeats. Use for rhythmic dotted-eighth parts, clear echoes and modern ambient layers.
delay|Dual Delay: Two independent delay lines in one block, each with its own time and feedback. Useful for complex rhythmic patterns or wide stereo echoes.
delay|Dual Reverse Delay: Two reverse delay lines, playing chunks of your signal backwards. Creates swelling, psychedelic, backwards-guitar textures with extra width.
delay|Simple Ping Pong Delay: Straightforward stereo delay whose repeats bounce between left and right. Great for wide, spacious rhythmic echoes.
delay|Reverse Delay: Records and plays back your signal in reverse. Delivers backwards swells for psychedelic leads and ambient textures.
delay|Simple Delay: No-frills digital delay with the essential controls. Quick to dial for everyday echo duties.
delay|Tape Delay: Emulation of a tape echo with warm, saturated, slightly wobbly repeats. Ideal for vintage slapback, dub echoes and lo-fi character.
delay|Circular Delay: Delay that outputs a patterned 'chunk' of syncopated repeats chosen by a Tap Preset, circling gradually around the stereo field. For rhythmic patterns a normal single delay can't produce.
delay|Arpeggio Delay: A multi-tap delay where each repeat gets its own pitch and stereo position. Turns single notes into melodic echoes and evolving arpeggiated patterns.
delay|Crystal Delay: Produces bright, shimmering, pitched-up repeats that sit above the original signal. Great for ethereal leads and ambient swells.
reverb|Ambience: Short, subtle reverb that adds space without an obvious tail. Use it to make a dry tone sound like it's in a real room.
reverb|Blossom (ST): Stereo reverb inspired by the Strymon BigSky's Bloom mode: lush tails that swell and 'bloom' after the note. For ambient pads and cinematic textures.
reverb|Cave: Large, dark, cavernous reverb with long reflections. Ideal for atmospheric and dramatic effects.
reverb|Hall: Classic concert-hall reverb with smooth, long decay. A versatile choice for leads, cleans and ballads.
reverb|Mind Hall: Large, lush, modulated hall-style reverb with an expansive, dreamy character. Suited to ambient and post-rock soundscapes.
reverb|Modulated: Reverb with modulation in the tail for a chorused, swirling decay. Adds movement to cleans and ambient parts.
reverb|Nordic Concert Hall (ST): Stereo reverb inspired by Valhalla VintageVerb's Concert Hall mode: a smooth, vintage-digital hall. Big, polished space for leads and cleans.
reverb|Plate: Emulation of a classic studio plate reverb: bright, dense, smooth. The studio standard for vocals and guitar.
reverb|Plate Lush: Plate reverb variant with a longer, richer, more lush tail. For big, washy ballad and ambient sounds.
reverb|Plate Tight: Plate reverb variant with a shorter, tighter decay. Adds sheen without clutter for rhythm parts.
reverb|Room: Natural room reverb simulating small-to-medium spaces. Makes an amp sound 'in the room' rather than direct.
reverb|Shimmer: Reverb with pitch-shifted (typically octave-up) feedback for an angelic, choir-like shimmer. A staple of ambient and worship guitar.
reverb|Spring (M): Mono spring reverb emulating the drippy, splashy tank in vintage amps. For surf, rockabilly and classic Fender-style cleans.
reverb|Spring (ST): Stereo version of the spring reverb emulation: vintage amp-tank drip with width.
reverb|Spring Reverb Engine (M): Mono, more detailed and tweakable spring reverb engine with extended controls over the spring tank's behaviour. For authentic vintage spring sounds.
reverb|Spring Reverb Engine (ST): Stereo version of the advanced spring reverb engine, with deep control over tank character and spread.
reverb|Studio Plate 70 (ST): Stereo reverb based on the Lexicon PCM70 Rich Plate programs: that '80s studio-rack plate sheen. Classic for polished lead and clean tones.
reverb|Vintage Digital: Based on the OTO Machines BAM Space Generator, recreating vintage digital reverb with lo-fi character, plus a Freeze function for infinite sustain pads.
compressor|Chief CS3: Model of the BOSS CS-3 Compression Sustainer: squishy pedal compression with added sustain. Classic for funk, country chicken-picking and even-sounding cleans.
compressor|Jewel: Model of the Diamond Compressor: a transparent optical-style pedal comp with a tilt EQ. Evens out dynamics subtly while keeping pick attack.
compressor|Legendary 87: Model of the Universal Audio 1176 FET studio compressor: fast, punchy, aggressive. Great for snappy attack and in-your-face guitar or bass.
compressor|Legendary 87 (ST): Stereo version of the 1176-based compressor, for stereo rigs and post-effects compression.
compressor|Legendary 87 (S/C): Sidechain version of the 1176-based compressor: its detector can be triggered by another signal (e.g. a separate input), for ducking and pumping effects.
compressor|Opto Comp: Optical-style compressor with smooth, program-dependent, musical response (LA-2A-flavoured). Gentle levelling for cleans and bass.
compressor|Opto Comp (ST): Stereo version of the optical-style compressor.
compressor|Opto Comp (S/C): Sidechain version of the optical-style compressor, triggered by another signal source for ducking effects.
compressor|Solid State Comp: Model of the SSL Bus compressor: the classic 'glue' compressor from SSL consoles. Adds cohesion and punch at the end of a chain.
compressor|Solid State Comp (ST): Stereo version of the SSL Bus-based compressor, ideal as a final stereo glue stage.
compressor|Solid State Comp (S/C): Sidechain version of the SSL Bus-based compressor, keyed from another signal for ducking/pumping.
compressor|VCA Comp: Clean, precise VCA-style compressor with fast, controlled response. Good for tightening dynamics transparently.
compressor|VCA Comp (ST): Stereo version of the VCA-style compressor.
compressor|VCA Comp (S/C): Sidechain version of the VCA-style compressor, driven by an external/secondary signal.
compressor|Douglas Shining Comp (M): New in 4.1.0 (mono): based on the Darkglass Hyper Luminal, a bass-focused compressor with VCA/FET-style modes. Handles both subtle levelling and pronounced squash.
pitch|Aggi Sub Octaver: Model of the Aguilar Octamizer: an analog-style octave-down that adds a clean sub octave. Fattens bass and baritone-style riffs.
pitch|Chief OC2: Model of the BOSS OC-2 Octave: classic analog one- and two-octave-down tracking. Thick, synthy low end for bass and guitar riffs.
pitch|Minivoicer: Compact harmonizer adding intelligent pitch-shifted voices to your signal. For quick harmony leads and thickening.
pitch|Pitch Correction: Pitch-correcting effect that snaps notes toward a chosen key/scale, including hard auto-tune-style robotic effects.
pitch|Pitch Shifter: General pitch shifter to transpose your signal by fixed intervals, mixed with the dry signal. For octaves, fifths, and harmony layers.
pitch|Poly Octaver: Model of the Electro-Harmonix POG: polyphonic octave generator with sub and upper octaves. Creates organ-like, 12-string and huge layered tones.
pitch|Subharmonic Synth: Model of the DOD Meatbox SubSynth: generates deep subharmonic frequencies under your notes. Massive sub bass for bass guitar and drop tunings.
pitch|Transpose: Full-wet pitch shift of your whole signal, like a virtual capo or drop-tuning. Play in a different key or tuning without retuning.
pitch|Wham: Model of the DigiTech Whammy: expression-controlled pitch bends, dive bombs and harmonies. The classic Tom Morello/Jack White pitch pedal.
pitch|Multivoicer: From Archetype: Tim Henson X, now free. Adds up to four pitch-shifted voices for rich, layered harmonies and arpeggios.
modulation|Chief CE2W: Model of the BOSS CE-2W (Waza Craft CE-2): warm, lush, analog BBD chorus. The classic '80s chorus for cleans and shimmering leads.
modulation|Chief CE2W (M): Mono version of the BOSS CE-2W-based chorus.
modulation|Chief DC2W: Model of the BOSS DC-2W Dimension C: subtle, spacious stereo chorus without obvious wobble. Widens tones while staying clean and natural.
modulation|Chief DC2W (M): Mono version of the BOSS DC-2W Dimension-based chorus.
modulation|Chorus 229T: Model of the TC Electronic TC 2290's chorus: the pristine, hi-fi rack chorus of '80s session players. Clean, wide shimmer.
modulation|Chorus Engine: Neural DSP's deep, fully tweakable chorus engine. Dial anything from subtle thickening to heavy warble.
modulation|Digital Flanger: Clean digital flanger with a crisp, jet-like sweep. For classic swoosh effects and metallic textures.
modulation|Dream Chorus: Model of the TC Electronic Dreamscape (John Petrucci's signature chorus/flanger pedal): lush, wide chorus. Great for clean arpeggios.
modulation|Dream Chorus (M): Mono version of the TC Dreamscape-based chorus.
modulation|Dual Chorus: Two chorus voices for a thicker, wider stereo chorus. For big, lush clean tones.
modulation|Flanger Engine: Neural DSP's deep, tweakable flanger engine. From subtle comb-filter movement to extreme jet sweeps.
modulation|Flangerish: Neural DSP's flanger with a classic, musical sweep. Quick-to-dial flanging for rock and psych tones.
modulation|Harmonic Tremolo: Emulation of the harmonic tremolo in early-'60s Brownface Fender amps: splits highs and lows and modulates them out of phase for a phasey, swirling pulse.
modulation|Micro Processor (ST): Stereo effect based on the Eventide MicroPitch Delay: micro pitch detune plus delay for wide, doubled, chorus-like widening. A studio favourite for stereo width.
modulation|MX Flanger: Model of the MXR M117R Flanger: rich, analog, jet-plane flanging. Classic Van Halen-era swoosh.
modulation|MX Phase 95: Model of the MXR Phase 95, combining the Phase 45 and Phase 90 (plus script mode). Classic swirling phase for funk, rock and leads.
modulation|MX Vibes: Model of the MXR Uni-Vibe: throbbing, chorus/phaser-like pulse with a lopsided sweep. The Hendrix/Trower/Gilmour vibe sound.
modulation|Pattern Tremolo: Tremolo that chops volume in programmable rhythmic step patterns rather than a smooth wave. For stuttering, sequenced gate-like rhythms.
modulation|Phaser: Neural DSP's phaser with adjustable stages and sweep. Classic swirling phase-shift modulation.
modulation|Rotary: Emulation of a rotating Leslie-style speaker cabinet with slow/fast rotor. For organ-like swirl on guitar and keys.
modulation|Tremolo: Classic amplitude tremolo that pulses your volume. For vintage surf, country and atmospheric parts.
modulation|Vibrato: Pitch vibrato that wobbles the pitch periodically (fully wet). For warbly, seasick, lo-fi and vintage vibrato tones.
modulation|Vintage Chorus: Warm, analog-flavoured chorus. Simple, classic chorus for cleans.
morph|Bit-Crusher (ST): Stereo bit-crusher that reduces bit depth and sample rate for lo-fi, digital grit. For glitchy, 8-bit and destroyed textures.
morph|Bit-Crusher Engine (M): Mono bit-crusher engine with deeper control over sample-rate and bit reduction. For lo-fi and aliasing effects.
morph|Freeze: Captures and holds a slice of your sound indefinitely as a sustained pad. Play over a frozen chord or create ambient drones.
morph|Phase-Locked Loop: Based on the EarthQuaker Devices Data Corrupter: a PLL harmonizing fuzz/synth that tracks your pitch and generates square-wave synth voices. Wild, glitchy monophonic synth tones.
morph|Glitch: From Archetype: Misha Mansoor X, now free. A granular delay that chops your signal into repeating patterns, from subtle movement to heavily distorted textures.
morph|Ring Modulator: Multiplies your signal with a carrier oscillator for metallic, bell-like, inharmonic tones. For sci-fi and experimental effects.
filter|Env. Filter: Envelope filter (auto-wah) whose sweep follows your picking dynamics. For funk 'quack' and bass synth tones.
filter|Env. filter (S/C): Sidechain version of the envelope filter: the sweep is triggered by a different signal than the one being filtered.
filter|Foog: Model of the Moog Moogerfooger MF-101 Low-Pass Filter: resonant Moog ladder filter with envelope follower. For synthy, funky and vowel-like filtering.
filter|Love Meat: Model of the Lovetone Meatball: a highly tweakable envelope filter. Deep, squelchy funk and synth-like auto-wah sounds.
eq|Graphic-9: 9-band graphic EQ for broad tone shaping. Sculpt mids, tame fizz or add low end quickly.
eq|Low-High Cut: Simple high-pass and low-pass filter. Remove rumble and fizz; essential for cleaning up mixes.
eq|Parametric-3: 3-band parametric EQ with adjustable frequency, gain and Q. For precise, surgical tweaks.
eq|Parametric-8: 8-band parametric EQ for detailed studio-grade shaping.
eq|Plugin Graphic-9: Graphic EQ matching the exact controls/ranges of the Archetype plugins' graphic EQ. Use it to recreate plugin presets accurately.
eq|Plugin Parametric-4: Four-band parametric EQ with high-pass and low-pass filters, matching the plugins' parametric EQ, for precise tone shaping.
wah|Auto Wah: Wah that sweeps automatically via LFO or envelope, no expression pedal needed. For funky, rhythmic wah.
wah|Bad Horse: Model of the Morley Bad Horsie (Steve Vai signature): optical, switchless wah with a wide, vocal sweep.
wah|Bass Wah: Wah voiced for bass with a lower sweep range, keeping low end intact.
wah|Bubba Wah: Model of the Dunlop Budda Budwah: smooth, vocal wah with a wide range and warm character.
wah|Crying Clyde Wah: Model of the Dunlop Cry Baby Clyde McCoy: vintage-voiced wah with a vocal, throaty sweep. Classic '60s wah.
wah|Crying Wah: Model of the Dunlop Cry Baby GCB-95: the standard, bright, classic rock wah.
wah|Crying Wah From Hell: Model of the Dunlop Crybaby From Hell (Dimebag Darrell signature): wide-range, aggressive wah with boost. Metal leads.
looper|Looper X: Full-featured looper with overdub, undo, reverse, half-speed and quantization. For practice, songwriting and live looping.
synth|Mono Synth: A free, enhanced version of the Overlord Synth from Archetype: Rabea X. Monophonic guitar-driven synth for leads and bass lines.
utility|Adaptive Gate: Noise gate that adapts to your signal, adjusting threshold dynamically. Keeps high-gain tones quiet between notes.
utility|Adaptive Gate (S/C): Sidechain version of the adaptive gate: it can listen to the clean input (before the amp) to gate the distorted signal more precisely.
utility|Gain: Simple level control. Boost or cut signal level anywhere in the chain.
utility|Simple Gate: Basic noise gate with threshold. Silences hiss and hum.
utility|Utility Gate: Noise gate with fuller controls (threshold, attack, release, etc.) for precise noise control.
utility|Volume: Volume block, usually assigned to an expression pedal for volume swells and level control.
utility|Phase Doctor: Inspired by the Little Labs IBP Phase Alignment Tool: adjusts phase between parallel paths to fix phase cancellation when blending signals or cabs.
utility|Plugin Gate: Noise gate matching the Archetype plugins' gate, for accurate recreation of plugin presets.
utility|Doubler: Creates a double-tracked effect, simulating two guitar takes for width. In 4.1.0 an INPUT three-way switch was added.
utility|Plugin Doubler: Doubler matching the Archetype plugins' doubler exactly. In 4.1.0 an INPUT three-way switch was added.
utility|Plugin Blend: Blends a signal from elsewhere in the chain in parallel with the processed signal, with the plugins' fixed EQ/compression; for recreating plugin presets. 4.1.0 added a BLEND LEVEL knob.
utility|Transparent Blend: Blends a signal from another point in your chain (e.g. the direct input) with the processed signal, transparently. 4.1.0 added a BLEND LEVEL knob.
